key_insight: An NLP pipeline using Bio_ClinicalBERT can identify brain metastases in radiology reports, including asynchronous cases that cancer registries often miss.
clinical_relevance: This could support scalable population-level surveillance of brain metastases and improve registry completeness for neuro-oncology planning.
method: Trained two Bio_ClinicalBERT models on radiology report sections: Findings and Impressions.
Combined section outputs by taking the maximum predicted probability as the report-level prediction.
Validated internally and externally across Canadian provinces using manually labeled reports.
evidence_signal: The model was trained on 1,879 samples and internally tested on 1,833 reports from 357 patients, reaching sensitivity 0.888 at a 0.4 threshold and showing external sensitivity of 0.918 in Ontario and 0.726 in British Columbia.
watch_item: Performance varied by province and precision was modest, so site-specific validation and workflow integration are important before broad deployment.
paper_title: Natural Language Processing Based Solution for Labeling Brain Metastasis Identified in Radiology Reports
